title: RACER-GT: Randomized Acquisition, Calibration, Error Decomposition, and Reliability for Google Trends
description:
A design-based statistical framework and Python package for constructing long-horizon daily Google Trends relative-search-interest indices from repeated, separately normalized retrievals.

RACER-GT treats data acquisition as a preregistered repeated-measurement experiment rather than a preliminary inconvenience. Global overlap-graph weighted least squares replaces sequential stitching and removes error accumulation; exact and near-duplicate diagnostics prevent dependent retrievals from being counted as independent evidence; a three-facet generalizability decomposition separates historical date, collection day and collection stream; a covariance-adjusted consensus reports an honest effective sample size; and the resulting measurement uncertainty is propagated into reliability-corrected OLS and SIMEX.

The package does not estimate absolute Google search counts. All unbiasedness, consistency and minimum-variance results are conditional on assumptions stated explicitly in the accompanying methodology manuscript, which is distributed in Traditional Chinese and English.
